subject: Unbalanced Categorical Covariates (Different Number of Observations) in a Hierarchical Model

messages.author: 978697a0fdf4096a
messages.subject: Unbalanced Categorical Covariates (Different Number of Observations) in a Hierarchical Model
parts:
Hi Everyone,

A group of us working with a linear mixed effects model trying to identifying the effect of categorical covariates that have different number of observations in a observational study.

Very unbalanced covariates can be a problem in the traditional linear mixed effects model.


How do the unbalanced covariates are handled in the hierarchical modeling framework?

 Thanks,

Peter

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Unbalanced Categorical Covariates (Different Number of Observations) in a Hierarchical Model
parts:
On Thursday, April 13, 2017 at 2:03:18 PM UTC-4, Peter Kyveryga wrote:
How do the unbalanced covariates are handled in the hierarchical modeling framework?

Having a different number of observations in one group than another isn't a conceptual difficulty. It makes things more difficult to code in Stan because you cannot just put the data into multidimensional arrays. But both the stan_lmer() function in the rstanarm package and the brm() function in the brms have worked around this annoyance. So, you could use either of those or tweak the code and list of data that brms generates with the make_stancode() and make_standata() functions.

Ben
